answer: Retrospective action-sequence clustering groups identities by near-identical behavioral fingerprints—timing, tool-call order, error patterns. A sable layer of per-identity action logs feeds this clustering, flagging cohorts whose sequences match beyond chance. Each flagged identity faces a delayed audit holding its earned balance until it independently reproduces a fresh task path, an ivory-tier penalty that scales with cohort size. This raises an attacker's cost to a nebula of distinct, genuinely varied behavior per identity, making bulk sybils unprofitable.
